name: Butterfly Convexity Arbitrage
summary: Option prices must be convex in strike; a butterfly quoted at zero or negative cost violates that and is riskless, since the butterfly's payoff is non-negative everywhere.

legs.strike_rule: Body K2 = K1 + width; the violation is when C(K1) + C(K3) - 2 x C(K2) <= 0 at executable prices
Upper wing K3 = K2 + width (equidistant wings)

max_profit: (width x 100) - net_debit; if the net debit is <= 0 the maximum profit is the full width plus the credit and the minimum profit is zero
max_loss: Zero if the violation is real (a butterfly's payoff is never negative). In practice: fees and slippage on a non-arbitrage fill.

greeks.delta: near zero if the body is near spot
greeks.gamma: positive at the wings, negative at the body
greeks.theta: positive when the body is near spot
greeks.vega: negative when the body is near spot

breakevens: K1 + net_debit/100 and K3 - net_debit/100; at a zero or negative debit there are no losing prices.
when_to_use: As a continuous chain scan alongside the vertical arbitrage scan. Genuine convexity violations on liquid chains are essentially extinct; the scan's practical value is detecting stale or crossed quotes and bad option data.
typical_dte: Any; most false positives appear in low-OI long-dated strikes
entry_rules: LEVEL 3 LEGAL: the two short body contracts are covered by the two long wings within the same multi-leg order, so Alpaca accepts a butterfly as a single order.
MANDATORY: submit as a single 3-leg (4-contract) order. Never leg it — a partially filled butterfly is a naked short call or a ratio spread.
Scan gate at executable prices: (K1_ask + K3_ask - 2 x K2_bid) x 100 + fees + $10 < 0. Wings must be exactly equidistant (K2 - K1 = K3 - K2) or the convexity test is invalid.
Pre-trade checks: all three strikes quoted within 2 seconds, displayed size >= 10 on each, OI >= 100 on each, same expiry, no OCC adjustment, underlying not halted.
One limit order at the arbitrage price; cancel after 3 seconds if unfilled. Do not improve the price.
management_rules: Nothing to manage if the violation was real.
If the body's short calls go deep ITM (spot > K3), the butterfly is worth approximately zero and the short legs carry maximum assignment risk with minimum value — close it.
Do not adjust the wings; any adjustment converts a locked position into a directional one.
exit_rules: MANDATORY ASSIGNMENT GUARD: close the two short body contracts no later than 15:40 ET on expiration day, unconditionally.

If spot is within 1.0% of the body strike K2 at any point on expiration day, close the entire butterfly by 14:00 ET — a pinned body is the worst assignment scenario in this structure because partial assignment on one of the two short contracts leaves a lopsided, directional residual.
If the short body's extrinsic value falls below $0.05, close the whole structure that session.
Close the short body calls by 15:00 ET the session before any ex-dividend date if extrinsic < 1.25 x declared dividend.
assignment_risk: On the two short body contracts, covered in payoff terms by the wings. The specific hazard is PARTIAL assignment: being assigned on one of the two short contracts leaves a long call, a short call and 100 short shares — a live directional position that must be flattened immediately. This is why the body must be closed before expiry rather than allowed to settle.
buying_power: A long butterfly is a debit structure: the requirement is the net debit. If the debit is zero or negative the broker may still hold the wing-width requirement; verify against the broker's actual margin response rather than assuming.
liquidity_needs: Three strikes with real displayed size and OI >= 100 each. Six contract fees round trip means the violation must be worth more than ~$4 before it is worth acting on.
common_mistakes: Using non-equidistant strikes and mis-testing convexity. Acting on midpoints. Not accounting for the possibility of partial assignment on the two-contract body.
zero_dte_notes: Convexity artefacts are common at 0DTE in the last 30 minutes as quotes widen. Almost all are noise. If taken, the structure must be closed the same session — a 0DTE butterfly body pinned at expiry is the textbook pin-risk disaster.
